stages.title: Dynamic efficiency and X-inefficiency
stages.sub: Understand how competition (or the lack of it) affects costs over time and innovation.

steps.q: A firm faces many rivals who all sell the same product cheaply. If this firm lets its costs creep up, what happens to its customers?
steps.hint: With lots of close rivals, what stops a firm getting lazy about costs?

steps.right: The lowest possible cost of producing its output
steps.wrong: The highest possible output regardless of cost

steps.q: A firm with tough rivals ploughs profits into new machinery and R&D year after year, hoping to cut costs further in future. What is it doing with its money now?
steps.right: Investing it to improve products and processes over time
steps.wrong: Holding onto it to keep costs the same
steps.hint: Is the firm reacting to today's costs, or preparing for future ones?

steps.wrong: The same efficiency, just repeated each year
steps.hint: Compare the firm now with the firm five years ago, not with a rival today.

steps.q: Now picture a firm with no real rivals at all, protected from competition. Its managers stop bothering to check for waste. What happens to its costs compared to the lowest possible?
steps.right: Costs rise above the lowest possible level
steps.wrong: Costs stay at the lowest possible level
steps.hint: Without rivals to punish waste, what keeps the firm's costs down?
